hooks.name: Nonverbal Dominance
hooks.hook: A sigh or an eye roll, specifically timed to a moment you speak up.
hooks.note: Trimming the candidate dropped the timing, which is the recognisable part.
hooks.review_note: The one hook I am holding back, and the ground is narrow. The composed line is 'A sigh or an eye roll, timed exactly to the moment you speak up.' The book's own sentence reads 'specifically timed to a moment the target speaks up or disagrees'; the composed version upgrades 'specifically' to 'exactly' and 'a moment' to 'the moment'. That is an intensifier the drafter added rather than inherited, and it asserts precision of timing — which is the observable proxy for deliberateness — as settled fact. It matters here more than it would elsewhere because this entry's entire false-positive risk is involuntary expression: the codex entry's own disconfirming case, which I approved, says 'Faces move on their own: a flash of visible irritation, an expressive manner, a real sigh at the end of a long day', and it disproportionately protects neurodivergent people, people in pain, and people who are simply tired. A hook is the most detachable and most screenshotted fragment of a clip, and this one overshoots the guard its own entry supplies. A fix needs to drop the intensifier; the drafter's stated reason for composing — that trimming lost the timing, which is the recognisable part — is fully satisfied by the book's weaker wording, so no new material is needed. I am flagging this as the mildest of my three holds and would not object if the editor resolved it by reverting to the book's phrasing verbatim. [Fixed 2026-08-27: reverted to the book's own wording ("specifically timed" not "timed exactly"), per the review's explicit recommendation. Re-approved.]

hooks.name: Resource Sabotage
hooks.hook: Resources or support that were previously available are quietly withdrawn.
hooks.review_note: A described situation in the passive, reporting a withdrawal without naming who withdrew. The trim drops 'right before they'd be needed for something important', losing some of the timing implication; acceptable, and again the more neutral choice.

hooks.name: Malicious Compliance
hooks.hook: A task completed in a way that satisfies the literal words of a request.
hooks.review_note: A described situation. Notably the trim stops before the source's 'while clearly defeating its purpose', which removes the strongest implication of intent — appropriate for a Watch-only entry where the codex text explicitly says text alone cannot establish intent.

hooks.name: Spiritual Bypassing
hooks.hook: Forgiveness or "letting go" is demanded on a spiritual or moral basis.
hooks.review_note: A described situation naming the entry's actual discriminator — the demand for forgiveness on a spiritual basis — while remaining silent on whether the belief is sincere. That is the correct line for a religiously sensitive entry and matches the codex text's care.

hooks.name: Ritualized Exhaustion
hooks.hook: A schedule that leaves little to no time for rest, reflection, or recovery.
hooks.review_note: A described situation about a schedule, which is factual and checkable. Drops the source's 'sustained over an extended period', which is a real loss of the duration qualifier, though the codex entry carries it; a style rather than clinical concern.

hooks.name: Moral Licensing
hooks.hook: "I'm one of the good ones."
hooks.review_note: Quoted speech, five words, instantly recognisable. Reports a claim someone made about themselves rather than evaluating whether it is true, which is the right form.

hooks.name: Smart-Home Coercion
hooks.hook: References to information a connected device would have captured.
hooks.note: Dropped the parenthetical '(movements, conversations)' as well as the trailing clause.
hooks.review_note: A described situation. Reports references to information a device would have captured — an observation the viewer can make directly — without asserting the device was actually used to obtain it. Appropriately hedged for a technical entry where malfunction is a real alternative.

hooks.name: Spatial Invasion
hooks.hook: Positioning between the target and an exit, or in a doorway.
hooks.review_note: A described situation, physical and concrete. Reports positioning without asserting purpose, which is right given the codex entry's concession that small rooms and crowded venues force closeness on everyone.

hooks.name: Willful Blindness as Complicity
hooks.hook: Clear warning signs are consistently not investigated further.
hooks.review_note: A described situation in the passive, retaining the source's recurrence qualifier ('consistently'). It drops 'by someone whose position would normally call for a closer look', which is the clause establishing a duty to inquire — a real loss of precision, though not one that creates an accusation. Style rather than clinical.

codex_fields.name: Weaponized Incompetence
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The task lands permanently on one person, along with the work of noticing it, asking about it, and eventually giving up on asking. Raising it also makes them sound as if they are complaining about help they were offered.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. The drafted why_this_matters stays entirely on cost-to-the-affected-person — the task landing permanently plus the meta-labour of noticing and re-asking — and never characterises the other party's capability, which is the exact trap on a neurodivergence-flagged entry where genuine skill gaps and ADHD executive difficulty produce the identical surface. The second sentence ('sounds as if they are complaining about help they were offered') names a real double bind without asserting anyone engineered it. Correctly scoped: what_it_is_not was left null because the book's existing field already carries the disability/ADHD caveat, and duplicating it here would have been the drafter overwriting a stronger existing line.

codex_fields.name: Strategic Apathy
codex_fields.why_this_matters: One person makes every decision alone and then carries the criticism for whichever way it went. Over time, deciding stops feeling like having a say and starts feeling like exposure.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. 'Deciding stops feeling like having a say and starts feeling like exposure' is a precise and clinically recognisable description of decision-fatigue-under-blame, and it describes the affected person's experience only. Critically for this entry, nothing in the draft implies the indifference is feigned — which matters because depression, burnout and decision fatigue produce identical sentences sincerely, as the book's own retained field says.

codex_fields.name: Reverse Psychology
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target's own resistance is what does the deciding, so a choice that felt like their own defiance may not have been theirs at all.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. The draft makes one specific and defensible point — that a choice experienced as one's own defiance may have been shaped — and stops there rather than asserting anyone set it up. Given how thoroughly playful challenge and honest doubt overlap with this in text, the restraint is the right call; the line survives even if the other party had no agenda at all.

codex_fields.name: Malicious Compliance
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target absorbs the failure with no clear grievance available to them: the instruction was followed, so there is nothing they can point at without sounding unreasonable.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. Well judged: the cost identified is the absence of an available grievance ('the instruction was followed, so there is nothing they can point at'), which is a structural fact about the situation rather than a claim about anyone's motive. This is the entry where the source definition itself contains 'deliberately designed to produce failure'; the draft conspicuously declines to inherit that intent language, which is the correct direction of travel.

codex_fields.name: Moral Licensing
codex_fields.why_this_matters: A specific, current complaint goes unanswered because the conversation turns into a referendum on someone's overall goodness, which the target cannot win and did not raise.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. Accurately identifies the actual mechanism of harm — a specific current complaint being converted into an unwinnable referendum on overall goodness — and notes the affected person did not choose that frame. Non-pathologising and culturally safe: it says nothing about people who genuinely do have good track records, which matters where communal reputation is legitimately load-bearing.

codex_fields.name: Strategic Self-Deprecation / Performed Humility
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target arrives with a concern and leaves having provided reassurance. The thing they came to say never gets said, and they often feel unkind for having wanted to say it.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. 'The thing they came to say never gets said, and they often feel unkind for having wanted to say it' captures the reversal precisely and locates the cost in the unraised concern rather than in the other person's sincerity. Important on this entry, since authentic low self-esteem and habitual self-criticism produce the same behaviour with no strategy behind them; the draft never asserts the self-deprecation is performed.

codex_fields.name: Priming / Narrative Seeding
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target reads an event through a lens they never chose, and mistakes a supplied conclusion for their own judgement. The frame is hardest to question precisely because it arrived before the evidence did.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. 'Mistakes a supplied conclusion for their own judgement' is an accurate account of the anchoring effect, and the closing observation — that a frame is hardest to question because it arrived before the evidence — is genuinely illuminating rather than accusatory. Notably it never claims the earlier comment was timed on purpose, which is the only claim that would have been unsupportable.

codex_fields.name: Ambiguity as Weapon
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target can feel the exclusion but cannot point to it. Naming it out loud sounds paranoid, and staying quiet means carrying the doubt alone.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. This is the strongest of the Watch-only set: it validates the affected person's perception ('can feel the exclusion but cannot point to it') while explicitly acknowledging that naming it sounds paranoid — which is exactly the bind, and saying so out loud is protective rather than destabilising. No claim is made that the vagueness was cultivated.

codex_fields.name: Push-Pull
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target organises their attention around a temperature they cannot predict, and tends to read each cold spell as something they must have caused.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. Correctly frames this as a Pattern-only shape: the cost is organising attention around an unpredictable temperature, and the self-blame attribution ('read each cold spell as something they must have caused') is named as the affected person's inference rather than as fact. Nothing here would let a reader conclude a partner with fluctuating mental health is doing this deliberately.

codex_fields.name: Intermittent Reinforcement
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Effort keeps rising as the returns fall. The rarity of the good moments is exactly what makes them feel worth waiting for, so the pattern is self-sustaining.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. Accurate on the behavioural science — variable-ratio schedules do produce more persistent responding than continuous reinforcement — and the draft renders it as lived experience ('effort keeps rising as the returns fall') without invoking conditioning jargon or implying anyone is running a schedule on purpose. 'Self-sustaining' is the right word: it locates the mechanism in the structure, not in a person.

codex_fields.name: Breadcrumbing
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target stays available for a relationship that never arrives, holding a place open on the strength of contact that costs almost nothing to send.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. The cost is precisely identified as opportunity cost — holding a place open for something that never arrives — and the asymmetry noted ('contact that costs almost nothing to send') is an observation about effort, not about intent. Safe for a reader whose situation is in fact just someone genuinely busy.

codex_fields.name: Trauma Bonding
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Relief and harm come from the same source, so the target's strongest sense of closeness arrives directly after the worst treatment — and then becomes a reason to stay.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. Clinically sound and carefully worded: it describes the fusion of relief and harm and its consequence for staying, without pathologising the person who has bonded or implying weakness. The term is widely misused in popular writing to mean 'bonding over shared trauma'; this draft uses it correctly, in Dutton and Painter's sense of an attachment forged by intermittent abuse and relief. No what_it_is_not was drafted, which is right — the book's existing field already carries the 'ordinary conflict and repair' contrast.

codex_fields.name: Relief Bait
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Each round of kindness resets what the target can tolerate, so the baseline of acceptable treatment moves downward without them noticing it move.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. Identifies the specific harm as a moving tolerance baseline and — the important part — notes it moves 'without them noticing it move', which is an accurate account of habituation and explains why the person's own read is not a reliable instrument here. Says nothing about whether the kindness was sincere, which it cannot know.

codex_fields.name: Withholding
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Ordinary things — an answer, an acknowledgement, basic warmth — turn into rewards, and the target starts negotiating for what was previously free. Because nothing visible happened, there is nothing to describe to anyone else.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. Two distinct costs are correctly separated: the conversion of ordinary things into rewards, and the evidentiary problem ('nothing visible happened, there is nothing to describe to anyone else'). The second is what makes this hard to get help for, and naming it is protective. Nothing here would misread a partner who genuinely needs time before talking.

codex_fields.name: Dr. Jekyll/Mr. Hyde
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target has no witnesses. The version other people know makes their account of the other version sound implausible, including to themselves.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. 'The target has no witnesses' is the whole clinical point of this entry and the draft leads with it, then adds the corrosive part — that the account sounds implausible 'including to themselves'. That final clause is doing real work: it tells a reader that their own disbelief is a predictable feature, not evidence they are wrong. No character claim is made about the person with two presentations.

codex_fields.name: Ambient Abuse
codex_fields.why_this_matters: There is nothing to quote, so the exhaustion has no justification the target can offer to anyone, themselves included. They stay braced without being able to say what for.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. Correctly identifies that the defining feature is the absence of quotable material, and draws the right consequence — exhaustion with no justification the person can offer to anyone, themselves included. 'They stay braced without being able to say what for' is an accurate description of hypervigilance without using the clinical term or implying a diagnosis in either party.

codex_fields.name: Ghosting-Orbiting Cycle
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target is neither in contact nor free of it. Attention keeps arriving with no reply attached, which keeps hope alive at precisely the point it was starting to fade.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. 'Neither in contact nor free of it' is exactly right, and the specific harm named — attention arriving with no reply attached, sustaining hope at the point it was fading — is grounded in the entry's own examples. Makes no claim that the viewing is monitoring, which the source material also declines to make.

codex_fields.name: Stonewalling
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Every issue stays permanently open. The target cannot resolve it, cannot drop it, and cannot even find out when it might be discussed.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. The three-part bind (cannot resolve, cannot drop, cannot find out when) is accurate and is the clinically significant feature distinguishing this from someone needing processing time. Correctly avoids Gottman's prognostic framing, which would have imported a claim about the relationship's future that this entry cannot support.

codex_fields.name: Sealioning
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target's energy goes into sourcing and proving rather than into being heard, and the point they were trying to make is eventually abandoned for reasons of stamina.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. Locates the cost in redirected effort — sourcing and proving instead of being heard — and attributes the abandonment to stamina rather than to being wrong, which is the accurate causal account. Says nothing about the questioner's good faith, which matters given how completely genuine curiosity and this overlap in text.

codex_fields.name: Idealize-Devalue-Discard Cycle
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target measures the ending against the extraordinary beginning and concludes that they must have caused the decline — which is also the conclusion that keeps them trying to earn the beginning back.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. The most diagnosis-adjacent entry in the batch, and the draft handles it correctly: it never mentions narcissism or any personality construct, and instead describes the affected person's inference (that they caused the decline) and why that inference keeps them trying. Given how routinely this cycle is used in popular content as a de facto diagnostic checklist, keeping it purely descriptive is the right clinical call.

codex_fields.name: Extinction Bursts
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The first boundary that actually works is the one that costs the most, which teaches the target that holding a limit makes things worse rather than better.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. Behaviourally accurate — an extinction burst is a real and well-documented phenomenon — and the draft draws the genuinely useful implication: that the first effective boundary costs the most, which teaches the wrong lesson. This is protective information for someone about to conclude that holding a limit made things worse, and it is framed as a pattern property rather than as retaliation.

codex_fields.name: Competitive Victimhood
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target's own pain never gets a hearing, and rather than enter a contest they cannot win, they stop raising things at all.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. Correctly identifies the terminal cost — not the unfairness of the comparison but the withdrawal that follows ('they stop raising things at all'). Careful on a culturally sensitive axis: it does not suggest the other person's pain is fabricated or lesser, only that the affected person's never gets a hearing.

codex_fields.name: Ambient Sexual Threat
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target reorganises their movements, schedule and attention around one person while holding nothing concrete enough to report, or even to explain to a friend.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. Handles a genuinely difficult entry well: it validates the reorganisation of movement and schedule around one person while explicitly acknowledging there is nothing concrete enough to report — which is the actual predicament and is protective to state plainly. It does not tell the reader what to do, which is appropriate for a Pattern-only entry, though I flag separately in the report that this entry carries no safety_sensitive tag and arguably should.

codex_fields.name: "Polite Hostile" Environments
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Nothing that happens is documentable, so whoever spoke up carries the cost alone with no case to make. Everyone watching learns that silence is the sensible option.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. The second sentence — 'everyone watching learns that silence is the sensible option' — correctly identifies this as a systemic rather than dyadic harm, which is what distinguishes the entry from ordinary workplace friction. Non-accusatory toward civility norms themselves, which matters because the draft could easily have implied professionalism is itself suspect.

codex_fields.name: Self-Gaslighting Induction
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The doubting continues with nobody present to do it. The target discounts things they clearly remember and edits their own account before anyone has even challenged it.
codex_fields.review_note: Correctly written about an internalised state rather than an exchange: 'the doubting continues with nobody present to do it' is the defining feature and the draft leads with it. 'Edits their own account before anyone has even challenged it' is a precise description of anticipatory self-correction and carries no implication that the person is unreliable — the opposite.

codex_fields.name: Fawning
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Safety is bought with the target's own position: they apologise for things done to them, and lose track of what they actually think while they are still saying it.
codex_fields.review_note: Clinically correct and non-pathologising: it treats fawning as a cost paid ('safety is bought with the target's own position') rather than as a personality weakness, consistent with the source material's framing of it as a nervous-system response alongside fight/flight/freeze. 'Lose track of what they actually think while they are still saying it' is an accurate description of the in-the-moment dissociation from one's own position.

codex_fields.name: Self-Abandonment
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target can say what would keep the peace far more readily than what they want, and their own limits stop being information they are willing to act on.
codex_fields.review_note: The contrast it draws — being able to say what would keep the peace more readily than what one wants — is lifted from the entry's own example set and is a genuinely usable self-recognition cue. Ends on the right note clinically: limits stop being information the person is willing to act on, which frames the problem as access to one's own signal rather than as a character defect.

codex_fields.name: Internalized Conditioning
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The rules keep running in the other person's absence, so distance — even ending the relationship — no longer brings the relief the target expected it to.
codex_fields.review_note: The strongest observation in this sub-block: that distance or even ending the relationship no longer brings expected relief. That is both accurate and important for a reader who has left and is confused about why nothing improved, and it is grounded in the source's 'operating from inside your own head' framing. Does not imply the rules were installed on purpose.

codex_fields.name: Silence Installation
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The problems most in need of raising become the ones the target physically cannot raise, so they go unaddressed indefinitely and quietly grow.
codex_fields.review_note: Identifies the compounding harm correctly — the topics most needing to be raised are the ones that become unraisable, so they grow. Careful on the somatic claim: the source describes throat-closing and physical resistance, and the draft renders this as 'physically cannot raise' without escalating it into a medical assertion.

codex_fields.name: Approval Addiction Cultivation
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target's sense of how they are doing is outsourced to someone else's mood, and their own view of a thing arrives too late to count for much.
codex_fields.review_note: 'Their own view of a thing arrives too late to count for much' is a precise and original way of naming the sequencing problem, and it is grounded in the source's example of checking someone's reaction before knowing how you feel. Avoids the moralising that the entry's own name ('addiction') invites; the draft never suggests the person is weak-willed.

codex_fields.name: Parentification
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target treats their own needs as an imposition, and the growing-up that was postponed to keep an adult afloat does not happen later on its own.
codex_fields.review_note: Clinically accurate on both halves of the construct: the internalised sense of one's needs as an imposition, and the developmental cost. The final clause — that the postponed growing-up 'does not happen later on its own' — is a real and non-obvious clinical point about arrested development in parentified children, and it is stated as a fact about the process rather than as a prognosis for any reader.

codex_fields.name: Process Exhaustion
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target loses to depletion rather than to a decision, and the outcome is recorded as voluntary — they withdrew, they did not pursue it, they stopped replying.
codex_fields.review_note: The key insight is in the second clause: the outcome is recorded as voluntary ('they withdrew, they did not pursue it, they stopped replying'). That is an accurate and specific account of how attrition gets memorialised as consent, and it is the thing that makes this hard to challenge afterwards. Nothing here indicts ordinary procedural slowness.

codex_fields.name: HR Shielding
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The person who reported the harm absorbs the disruption while the situation they reported continues, and everyone else in the organisation learns what reporting costs.
codex_fields.review_note: Correctly identifies the two-level harm: the reporter absorbs disruption while the reported situation continues, and — the systemic half — everyone else learns what reporting costs. Fair to HR as a function: the draft describes an outcome pattern, not a claim that HR staff intend it, which matters given how routinely this entry's subject is used to discourage reporting altogether.

codex_fields.name: Pseudo-Consultation
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target spends real effort and real candour on input that could never have changed anything, and the decision is afterwards described as one they helped make.
codex_fields.review_note: Names the specific injury accurately — real effort and real candour spent on input that could not have changed anything — and adds the aggravating feature, that the decision is afterwards described as one they helped make. That second clause is what distinguishes this from ordinary disappointment at not getting your way.

codex_fields.name: Tokenism
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target's presence is used as the answer to the criticism they were brought in to voice, and objecting to that makes them look ungrateful for the seat.
codex_fields.review_note: 'Their presence is used as the answer to the criticism they were brought in to voice' is a tight and accurate statement of the structural bind, and the closing note about looking ungrateful for the seat identifies why it is rarely contested. Non-accusatory toward genuinely new roles, which the book's existing field covers.

codex_fields.name: Individualization of Systemic Issues
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target adds self-improvement to an already unsustainable load, and concludes that the shortfall is in their own resilience rather than in the conditions.
codex_fields.review_note: Correctly identifies the compounding cost — self-improvement added to an already unsustainable load — and the attributional error that follows, that the shortfall is read as a resilience deficit rather than a condition. This is an accurate description of the individualisation critique and is stated without implying any organisation intends it.

codex_fields.name: Diffusion of Responsibility
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The harm is real and nobody is answerable for it, so the target has nowhere to take it, no one to ask for repair, and no way to stop it recurring.
codex_fields.review_note: The three consequences named (nowhere to take it, no one to ask for repair, no way to stop recurrence) are the real practical harms of unaccountable systems, and framing it as 'the harm is real and nobody is answerable for it' correctly separates the outcome from anyone's culpability. Grounded in the source's 'perfect, unbreakable circle of non-responsibility'.

codex_fields.name: Deepfakes
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target is left disproving something that never happened, to people who have already seen it — and denial is exactly what a guilty person would also say.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY, safety_sensitive and playbook-risk. The why stays strictly on the affected person's position — disproving something to people who have already seen it — with no description of how synthesis is done or improved, so there is no instructional drift. The closing observation ('denial is exactly what a guilty person would also say') is the genuinely useful clinical point and is protective rather than despairing: it explains why the person's own denial feels ineffective, which pre-empts self-blame. Nothing discourages evidence-gathering or reporting.

codex_fields.name: AI Voice Cloning
codex_fields.why_this_matters: A voice the target has trusted their whole life stops being evidence of anything, and verifying every unexpected call through a second channel becomes a permanent tax on ordinary contact.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY, safety_sensitive. Frames the harm as the loss of a trusted signal ('a voice the target has trusted their whole life stops being evidence of anything') and correctly counts second-channel verification as a permanent cost rather than presenting it as a tidy solution — which is honest, and avoids the false reassurance that would be the real safety failure here. No technique detail whatsoever.

codex_fields.name: Doxxing
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Risk moves offline and out of the target's hands: their home, workplace and family become reachable by strangers who have no relationship to the original dispute, and the exposure cannot be reversed.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY, safety_sensitive. Correctly identifies the defining feature — risk moving offline and out of the person's hands — and names the irreversibility plainly rather than softening it. Naming that exposure cannot be reversed is the right call for a safety entry: it neither catastrophises nor implies the situation is manageable by the affected person alone, and it contains nothing that would help anyone do this.

codex_fields.name: Sock Puppets
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target argues against what looks like a consensus and concludes they are the outlier, when the numbers on the other side were never real.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY, safety_sensitive. The cost is precisely stated as an epistemic one — concluding you are the outlier when the numbers opposing you were not real — which is the actual psychological harm and is grounded in the source's 'appearance of independence' framing. Contains no operational detail about constructing or evading detection of such accounts.

codex_fields.name: Coordinated Reporting
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target loses their account, their reach, or their income through a system built to protect people, and there is no realistic appeal against a decision that was made on volume.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY, safety_sensitive. Accurately identifies the compounding injustice: loss of account, reach or income through a system built to protect people, with no realistic appeal against a decision made on volume. 'Made on volume' is the correct mechanism and is stated without instructing anyone in how to generate that volume. Livelihood loss is named without minimising it.

codex_fields.name: Credential-Costuming
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target defers to standing that is not there, and the questions they would otherwise have asked start to feel out of place. Decisions then rest on the appearance of expertise rather than on anything that was tested.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: An unfamiliar credential is not a false one — plenty of genuine titles mean nothing outside their field, and modest people describe real experience in ways that happen to sound grand. A claim you cannot place is something to check, not a finding in itself.
codex_fields.review_note: The why identifies a second-order cost that is easy to miss — that the questions the person would otherwise have asked 'start to feel out of place' — which is the actual mechanism of deference, not just the false claim itself. The disconfirming case genuinely holds: unfamiliar-but-real credentials and modest people describing real experience are both common, and 'a claim you cannot place is something to check, not a finding in itself' correctly downgrades the observation to a prompt rather than a conclusion.

codex_fields.name: Identity Performances
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Trust is extended to a version of someone that does not exist, so the target's read on the relationship rests on facts that were supplied to them rather than observed.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Everyone presents differently in different rooms, and someone rebuilding or still working out who they are is changing rather than fabricating. The question is whether specific claims hold up under a reasonable follow-up, not whether the person seems unlike themselves at work.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case does real work by separating two things that look alike from outside: someone rebuilding or still working out who they are, versus fabrication. The test offered — whether specific claims survive reasonable follow-up, rather than whether the person seems unlike themselves at work — is a genuinely usable discriminator and correctly protects ordinary code-switching, which is the main misapplication risk on this entry.

codex_fields.name: Social Engineering
codex_fields.why_this_matters: What gets used is the target's ordinary decency — helpfulness, deference to apparent authority, reluctance to make a fuss — so the loss afterwards feels like a personal failing rather than something done to them.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Genuinely urgent legitimate requests exist, and real IT or security staff follow processes that most people have never met before. Checking back through a channel you already trust costs an honest request nothing, which is why it is the cheap test here rather than suspicion of the person.
codex_fields.note: This entry sits closer to fraud than to relational manipulation, so the disconfirming case is framed around verification rather than around pattern-over-instance.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. The draft_note is accurate that this sits closer to fraud than relational manipulation, and framing the disconfirming case around verification rather than pattern-over-instance is the right structural choice. The why is the notable part: it identifies that what gets used is ordinary decency, and that the loss therefore feels like a personal failing — which is both clinically accurate about post-fraud shame and directly protective. 'Checking back through a channel you already trust costs an honest request nothing' is a sound test that does not require suspecting anyone.

codex_fields.name: Performative Allyship / False Solidarity
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Trust is given on the strength of stated values, and the gap only becomes visible at the moment support would have cost something — which is usually the moment the target most needed it.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Many people are further along in their stated values than in their practice and are genuinely, if unevenly, catching up. Quiet support that is never announced anywhere is the reverse of this pattern, not a mild version of it.
codex_fields.review_note: The why correctly locates the injury in timing — the gap becomes visible at the moment support would have cost something, which is usually the moment it was needed. The disconfirming case is unusually generous and better for it: it protects people whose practice lags their stated values and explicitly notes that unannounced private support is the reverse of this pattern, not a mild version of it, which forecloses the obvious misreading.

codex_fields.name: Punishment by Proxy
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target's own boundaries start carrying a cost for someone else, so protecting themselves means exposing a person they care about — which is usually enough to stop them.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Timing coincides far more often than intuition expects, and third parties have their own independent history with the same people. This is among the easiest patterns in the book to over-read and the least safe to act on from timing alone.

Because the tactic is defined by an inference about causation the reader usually cannot verify, the honest handling is to raise the bar, and the draft does: 'This is among the easiest patterns in the book to over-read and the least safe to act on from timing alone.' Naming a pattern as unsafe to act on is unusual in this genre and is the right clinical judgement. The why identifies a genuine coercive mechanism — self-protection requiring the exposure of someone else — without asserting anyone arranged it.

codex_fields.why_this_matters: The target's independent options close as their formal ones open, and any objection is answered by the fact that they were included.

The why captures the self-fulfilling loop: withdrawal is then read as proof of unwillingness.

codex_fields.why_this_matters: Because nothing quotable is ever said, the experience cannot be evidenced to anyone else, and the person on the receiving end often ends up self-editing around a reaction they could not describe if asked.

Note that the corresponding video hook for this entry overshoots this guard; that is flagged separately on the hook, not here.

codex_fields.why_this_matters: Failing without the tools needed to succeed reads to everyone watching — and often to the person themselves — as plain incompetence.

codex_fields.why_this_matters: A departure produced by these conditions looks, on paper and in memory, like a free choice — which leaves the person carrying the story that they simply could not cope.

codex_fields.why_this_matters: Losing independent access to your own email, money or messages turns ordinary daily life into something that has to be requested.

codex_fields.name: Health Sabotage
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Sleep, medication and medical care are the ground a person stands on to think and act; when those go, so does the capacity to notice what is happening or to leave.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: New babies, illness and crises wreck everyone's sleep and routines at once; transport, money and shift patterns genuinely get in the way of appointments; and someone struggling with their own health may be unable to help without doing anything to harm. codex_fields.review_note: This is the one codex entry I am holding back, and the problem is in what_it_is_not, not in why_this_matters, which is strong. The disconfirming case offers three innocent explanations — a new baby or crisis wrecking everyone's sleep, transport and money getting in the way of appointments, and a partner too unwell themselves to help — and then stops. Unlike every comparable high-stakes entry in this batch, it never names what would fall outside those explanations. Stalking & Surveillance closes with 'knowledge of details that were never shared through any of those channels'; Account Takeover closes with 'recovery attempts being blocked or intercepted'; Financial Dependence closes with 'what happens when the dependent person takes a step toward independence'. Health Sabotage has no equivalent, and the subject matter is medication, sleep and medical care — the domain where a person's capacity to think and to leave is most directly at stake. A reader whose medication is genuinely being interfered with can find all three explanations partly true of their circumstances (there really is a new baby, money really is tight, the other person really does have health problems) and be left with three exits and no door. That is the self-doubt failure mode this standard exists to catch, and it lands on the entry least able to absorb it. A fix needs to add a closing clause naming what the innocent explanations do not cover; the entry's own source material already supplies it — interference clustering 'around moments the target might otherwise assert independence' — so this requires no new claim, only the counterweight the rest of the set has. I would also expect this entry to carry a safety_sensitive flag, which it currently does not. The discriminator is precise and is about outcome rather than sincerity: tears while the conversation still continues are excluded; what marks the pattern is that accountability stops.

codex_fields.name: Obligation Installation
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Loyalty stops being something freely given and becomes a debt owed for having been trusted, and terms the person never agreed to can then be enforced as though they had.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Confiding in someone is how intimacy works, and mutual disclosure that is never later invoked as leverage is not this. Many relationship expectations go unstated and are still perfectly reasonable; the difference is being held to account for breaking a rule that was never available to see.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case affirms that confiding in someone is how intimacy works and that mutual disclosure never later invoked as leverage is not this — the right baseline. The distinguishing feature, being held to account for breaking a rule that was never available to see, is the accurate hinge and is stated without asserting anyone planted it.

codex_fields.name: Obligation Hooks
codex_fields.why_this_matters: A diffuse sense of owing colours every exchange, so even a reasonable refusal arrives feeling like a moral failure rather than a decision.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Relationships with a real history of give and take produce genuine feelings of reciprocity, and a personal tendency towards guilt or people-pleasing may be nobody's doing. Mutual obligation running in both directions is ordinary; one-directional and permanent is the shape to notice.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case correctly allows that a personal tendency toward guilt or people-pleasing 'may be nobody's doing' — an important exclusion, since this entry otherwise invites attributing one's own disposition to another person. The shape named, one-directional and permanent rather than mutual, is the right discriminator. The why captures the diffuseness that makes it hard to point at.

codex_fields.name: Loan-Sharking Gifts
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Accepting a kindness turns out to have been entering an agreement, with the price set later, by someone else, for something unrelated.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Generosity with no strings is common and looks identical at the moment of giving. Some people give freely as a matter of character and never mention it again. This one only becomes visible in retrospect, when the gift is produced as leverage for a separate demand.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case makes the honest structural admission that generosity with no strings 'looks identical at the moment of giving', so the entry can only be assessed retrospectively — and it says exactly that: 'This one only becomes visible in retrospect, when the gift is produced as leverage for a separate demand.' Conceding that no real-time test exists is better than inventing one.

codex_fields.name: Weaponized Generosity
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Witnesses to the favour raise the social cost of declining, so refusing what comes next means looking ungrateful in front of people who saw only the kindness.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Plenty of people are simply direct about wanting something back, and an openly transactional favour that survives a 'no' without consequence is not this. Reciprocal give and take between people who both understand the arrangement is ordinary.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case draws the right line at consequence rather than at expectation: an openly transactional favour 'that survives a "no" without consequence' is excluded, as is ordinary reciprocal give and take. That protects people who are simply direct about wanting something back. The why identifies the specific aggravating feature of witnesses raising the social cost of declining.

codex_fields.name: Guilt Legacy
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Repayment is expected for a debt incurred before the person could have consented to it, and declining reads as a betrayal not of one relationship but of a whole family line.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Family and cultural values around duty and reciprocity are genuinely held by many people who endorse them freely, and a parent recounting real history is sharing context rather than calling in a debt. Norms that differ from your own expectations are not the same as norms deployed as leverage for a specific present demand.
codex_fields.review_note: This is the entry with the greatest risk of cultural bias in the guilt block, and the draft handles it correctly. It affirms that family and cultural values around duty and reciprocity are genuinely held by many people who endorse them freely, and — the essential line — that norms differing from your own expectations 'are not the same as norms deployed as leverage for a specific present demand'. A parent recounting real history is explicitly sharing context rather than calling in a debt. The why correctly notes the debt was incurred before consent was possible.

codex_fields.name: Manufactured Intimacy
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Closeness arrives before there is any track record to justify it, so a person ends up trusting at a depth their actual knowledge of the other cannot support.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Some people open up quickly by temperament, and shared crises or intense circumstances genuinely accelerate bonding. Early disclosure can also be someone testing whether you can be trusted, which is a risk they are taking rather than one they are creating.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case is unusually thoughtful on the third exclusion: early disclosure can be someone testing whether you can be trusted, 'which is a risk they are taking rather than one they are creating'. That reframing is generous and correct. Temperament and crisis-accelerated bonding are also protected. The why identifies the mismatch between trust extended and knowledge held.

codex_fields.name: Manufactured Destiny
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Leaving stops feeling like ending a relationship and starts feeling like defying something larger, which raises the cost of an otherwise ordinary decision to go.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Strong early compatibility genuinely does feel remarkable to both people sometimes, and grand romantic language is a style in many cultures and individuals. Someone who sincerely believes in fate tends to say fated things about connections generally, not only about this one.
codex_fields.review_note: The discriminator offered is genuinely clever and observable: someone who sincerely believes in fate 'tends to say fated things about connections generally, not only about this one'. That is a consistency test that does not require judging anyone's sincerity. Grand romantic language is properly protected as a cultural and personal style. The why identifies the raised exit cost accurately.

codex_fields.name: Mirroring-on-Demand
codex_fields.why_this_matters: A sense of rare alignment forms with a reflection rather than a person, and what is later found to be missing was never actually there to lose.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Real compatibility, especially between people who met through a shared interest, produces genuine excitement at how much overlaps. An agreeable or accommodating style is not strategic reflection. The distinction lies in whether the shared enthusiasms have any independent history behind them, or appear complete and fully formed the moment they are mentioned.
codex_fields.review_note: The distinction drawn is the sharpest available for this entry: whether shared enthusiasms 'have any independent history behind them, or appear complete and fully formed the moment they are mentioned'. That is checkable. The disconfirming case properly protects real compatibility, especially between people who met through a shared interest, and agreeable communication styles. The why notes the loss was never actually there.

codex_fields.name: Pedestal Ploy
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Being the exception means having no peers, and worth becomes conditional on staying above the very people who might otherwise have offered perspective.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Specific admiration for someone's qualities isolates no one, and naturally complimentary people praise widely rather than comparatively. Two people bonding over feeling like outsiders together is ordinary — the flag is elevation that requires everyone else in the person's life to be worth less.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case correctly separates specific admiration, which isolates no one, from elevation that requires everyone else in the person's life to be worth less. That comparative structure is the actual mechanism and the right test. Two people bonding over feeling like outsiders together is properly excluded. The why identifies the loss of peers who might have offered perspective.

codex_fields.name: The Rescue Hook
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Substantial labour is given without ever having been asked for, so there is nothing to point at as an imposition and no clear moment at which it could have been declined.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: People genuinely struggle with specific skills, and someone raised without a task ever modelled to them has real rather than performed difficulty. An uneven division of tasks along the lines of who is better at what is normal in most households. The pattern is need that appears reliably rather than help that is asked for plainly.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case is careful about a real and common situation — someone raised without a task ever modelled to them has genuine rather than performed difficulty — and concedes that uneven division of tasks by aptitude is normal in most households. The discriminator, need that appears reliably rather than help asked for plainly, is behavioural. The why identifies labour given without a moment at which it could have been declined.

codex_fields.name: Premature Vulnerability
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Intense pain shared early creates a duty of care before there is any relationship to hold it, and stepping back then feels like abandoning someone in crisis.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Someone still living inside a recent loss will talk about it because it is present, not to accelerate anything. Others overshare from misreading the moment rather than from strategy. Early vulnerability that is mutual and reciprocated is how a good deal of real closeness begins.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case is compassionate and accurate: someone still living inside a recent loss will talk about it because it is present, not to accelerate anything, and others overshare from misreading the moment rather than from strategy. Noting that mutual early vulnerability is how a good deal of real closeness begins prevents the entry from making disclosure itself suspect. The why identifies a duty of care arriving before a relationship exists to hold it.

codex_fields.name: Emotional Parasitism
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Depletion accumulates so gradually that it registers as a personal failing — tiredness, low tolerance — rather than as the arithmetic of a relationship that never balances.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: A friend going through a genuinely hard stretch needs more for a while, and reciprocity resuming once things stabilise is ordinary. Someone with their own significant unmet needs may be unable rather than unwilling to give back. What distinguishes the pattern is an imbalance that is stable across years rather than weeks.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case makes the important clinical distinction that someone with significant unmet needs 'may be unable rather than unwilling to give back' — which keeps the entry from being used against people who are struggling. The discriminator is duration: an imbalance stable across years rather than weeks. The why is well observed on depletion registering as a personal failing rather than as arithmetic.

codex_fields.name: Information Control
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Outside perspectives that might have supplied a second opinion never arrive, so one account of events becomes the only one available to reason with.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Warning someone about a genuinely unreliable source is fair, and doing so without restricting their access to it is not control. A person who is simply uninformed themselves is filtering nothing. The distinguishing feature is what happens when the other person goes looking for a source independently.
codex_fields.review_note: The discriminator is precise and behavioural: what happens when the other person goes looking for a source independently. That separates warning someone about a genuinely unreliable source, which the disconfirming case affirms as fair, from restricting access. Noting that a person who is simply uninformed 'is filtering nothing' is a useful third exclusion.

codex_fields.name: Device Access Demands
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Refusing looks like concealment, so privacy has to be argued for rather than assumed, and the ordinary expectation of an unobserved thought quietly disappears.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Mutually agreed and revocable arrangements exist — shared family device management for young children, for instance — and clearly disclosed institutional requirements applied consistently to everyone are not personal. Voluntary transparency that both people want and either can end at any time is a different thing entirely.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case is well constructed around three conditions that actually matter — mutual agreement, revocability, and disclosed institutional requirements applied consistently. 'Voluntary transparency that both people want and either can end at any time is a different thing entirely' is the correct formulation, since revocability is the real variable. The why identifies the erosion of any expectation of unobserved thought.

codex_fields.name: Enforcing Trivial Demands
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Practising obedience on things that do not matter makes compliance on things that do feel like a smaller step than it is.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Particular preferences about how things are done are widespread and often just fussiness, and a rule with a real functional purpose can look arbitrary to someone who has not been told the reason. High standards in an area someone genuinely cares about are not a rehearsal for anything.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case correctly concedes that a rule with a real functional purpose 'can look arbitrary to someone who has not been told the reason' — a genuine and easily missed false positive — and protects high standards in an area someone cares about. The why states the mechanism accurately: practising obedience on things that do not matter makes compliance on things that do feel like a smaller step.

codex_fields.name: Boundary Testing
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Each step is too small to be worth a confrontation, which is precisely what allows the line to move without any single moment at which it could have been held.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: A one-off misjudgement with nothing following it is a mistake. Someone unclear where a line sits who adjusts once told has done exactly the right thing. Negotiating in good faith about where a reasonable boundary should sit is not testing it.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case is fair and specific: a one-off misjudgement with nothing following it is a mistake, someone unclear where a line sits who adjusts once told has done the right thing, and good-faith negotiation about where a boundary should sit is excluded. That third exclusion matters, since disagreement about a limit is not the same as probing it. The why identifies why no single moment presents itself for a confrontation.

codex_fields.name: Velvet Glove Control
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Nothing in the delivery offers anything to object to, so the narrowing of a person's choices happens while they feel well looked after.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Gentle guidance from someone who ultimately accepts a decision they disagree with is care, not control, and a soft-spoken manner conceals nothing by itself. The test sits at the point of refusal, not in how the request was phrased.
codex_fields.review_note: The test offered is exactly right and is the only one that works here: 'The test sits at the point of refusal, not in how the request was phrased.' That separates gentle guidance from control without making softness itself suspect, which the disconfirming case explicitly guards ('a soft-spoken manner conceals nothing by itself'). The why captures the disorienting part, that the narrowing happens while the person feels well looked after.

codex_fields.name: Demonstrating Omnipotence
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Resistance stops being attempted because it has already been made to look pointless, and that conclusion gets reached without anything having been tried.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Someone who genuinely has more reach or information in a particular area may simply be using it, and knowing something unexpected usually has an ordinary explanation. Being well-connected is not a display; what marks the pattern is capability shown for no purpose other than being seen.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case is appropriately deflationary, noting that knowing something unexpected usually has an ordinary explanation and that being well-connected is not a display. The discriminator is precise: capability shown 'for no purpose other than being seen'. The why identifies that resistance stops being attempted before anything is tried, which is the actual harm.

codex_fields.name: Forced Dependency
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The ability to manage alone is not lost through circumstance but never allowed to develop, so staying becomes the only workable option rather than the chosen one.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Differences in skill and interest naturally lead to one person handling certain things, and reasonable reliance during a genuine crisis is temporary by design. Someone who has decided they do not want to learn a task has made that choice. The difference is whether dependence reduces over time or is maintained.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case correctly protects the very common case of skill-and-interest differences leading one person to handle certain things, and — importantly — someone who has decided they do not want to learn a task 'has made that choice'. The discriminator is whether dependence reduces over time or is maintained, which is a trajectory test and the right one. The why distinguishes capability never allowed to develop from capability lost.

codex_fields.name: Golden Bars
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Comfort becomes an argument against leaving that has nothing to do with whether the arrangement is sound, and describing the situation to anyone else makes it sound enviable.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Unconditional generosity that would survive a disagreement is not a cage, and every major life decision involves real trade-offs that are fair to weigh openly. Material comfort being one honestly discussed factor among several in a mutual decision is ordinary.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case leads with a genuine test: generosity 'that would survive a disagreement is not a cage', which correctly makes conditionality rather than comfort the variable. It also concedes that every major life decision involves real trade-offs fair to weigh openly. The why notes the isolating effect of a situation that sounds enviable when described to anyone else.

codex_fields.name: Manufactured Scarcity
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Fear of losing the opportunity does the evaluating, and by the time there is room to think properly the decision has already been made.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Genuinely limited, time-sensitive opportunities exist, and their scarcity can usually be checked independently. Someone accurately reporting real stakes is not creating urgency. Deadlines that come from outside circumstances are not manufactured by whoever mentions them.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case correctly points out that genuine scarcity 'can usually be checked independently', which converts the entry into a verification prompt rather than a suspicion. Deadlines from outside circumstances are properly excluded as not manufactured by whoever mentions them. The why identifies that fear of loss does the evaluating before there is room to think.

codex_fields.name: Time Theft
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Hours are lost that cannot be recovered, and the message carried in the losing of them — that this person's time is not worth planning around — is absorbed long before it is ever named.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Occasional lateness from real circumstances, acknowledged and apologised for, is just life. Some people are chronically disorganised with everyone rather than with one person. Genuinely unpredictable work or caring commitments create real scheduling difficulty with no signal attached to it.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case makes a useful distributional point — some people are chronically disorganised with everyone rather than with one person — which is the right discriminator and mirrors the one used well in Interruption Patterns. Unpredictable work and caring commitments are excluded as creating real difficulty with no signal attached. The why identifies the message absorbed before it is named.

codex_fields.name: Deflection
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The original concern never receives a direct response, so it stays live and unaddressed while the conversation ends looking as though it happened.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Someone genuinely overwhelmed may need to pause and fully mean to come back, and a person who misunderstood the question will answer something adjacent to it. Dealing with a genuinely urgent related matter first is legitimate — the question is whether the original topic is ever actually returned to.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case is fair on all three exclusions and the third is the useful one: dealing with a genuinely urgent related matter first is legitimate, with the test being whether the original topic is ever actually returned to. That makes the pattern about return rather than about redirection. The why notes the concern stays live while the conversation ends looking as though it happened.

codex_fields.name: Apology Without Repair
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Each apology closes the incident without changing anything, so the same harm can recur indefinitely while the record shows it was addressed every time.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: A sincere apology followed by imperfect effort is how change usually looks — rarely instant, rarely linear. Some people apologise well and struggle with follow-through from a real skill gap rather than indifference. One relapse followed by re-commitment is not the pattern; an unbroken loop is.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case is clinically correct and generous about change: 'a sincere apology followed by imperfect effort is how change usually looks — rarely instant, rarely linear.' It also distinguishes a real skill gap in follow-through from indifference. The threshold named — one relapse followed by re-commitment is not the pattern; an unbroken loop is — is the right one and protects people genuinely trying.

codex_fields.name: Forced Forgiveness
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Resolution is claimed before acknowledgment, so the harm stays unprocessed and any further mention of it becomes the new problem.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: A mutual decision to move forward after real acknowledgment has already happened is repair, not pressure. Some people genuinely process conflict faster and do not require anyone else to match their pace. Family or cultural norms about not dwelling are not automatically avoidance.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case correctly protects two things: people who genuinely process conflict faster and do not require anyone to match their pace, and family or cultural norms about not dwelling, which 'are not automatically avoidance'. That cultural exclusion is important and is explicit. The discriminator is sequencing — resolution claimed before acknowledgment.

codex_fields.name: Plausible Deniability
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Every instance has an innocent reading available, so raising any one of them makes the person raising it look unreasonable, and the pattern can only be described by pointing at things that individually look like nothing.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: People do follow policy, and they do worry about others; often the innocent explanation is simply the true one. Someone being careful and honest can sound identical to someone producing cover. A single ambiguous incident cannot separate the two, which is why this belongs at the level of a pattern rather than an instance.
codex_fields.review_note: The most epistemically honest disconfirming case in the batch. It concedes that 'often the innocent explanation is simply the true one' and that someone being careful and honest 'can sound identical to someone producing cover', then draws the correct conclusion: a single ambiguous incident cannot separate the two, which is why this belongs at the level of a pattern rather than an instance. Admitting the indistinguishability at instance level is exactly right for this entry.

codex_fields.name: Feigned Ignorance
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Nothing can be settled, because the shared basis for settling it is unavailable, and whoever raised the issue ends up re-explaining rather than resolving.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Genuine forgetfulness, distraction and busy periods are universal, and a real gap in understanding on a specific topic is common. Confusion that tracks difficulty rather than convenience is not this; the pattern is normal comprehension everywhere except the inconvenient subject.
codex_fields.review_note: The discriminator is well chosen: 'confusion that tracks difficulty rather than convenience is not this' — the pattern being normal comprehension everywhere except the inconvenient subject. That selectivity test is checkable and does not require asserting anyone is pretending. Genuine forgetfulness, distraction and real gaps in understanding are properly excluded.

codex_fields.name: Victim Role Reversal
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Sympathy that would have gone to the person harmed goes elsewhere, and onlookers form an impression of the situation that is very hard to correct later.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Mutual harm is real, and two people can both have legitimate claims to being affected. Someone visibly wrestling with guilt is not necessarily redirecting anything. A person may also be genuinely going through something difficult that has nothing to do with the harm under discussion.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case makes the necessary concession that mutual harm is real and two people can both have legitimate claims to being affected, and that someone visibly wrestling with guilt 'is not necessarily redirecting anything'. That protects genuine remorse from being read as tactic. The why correctly identifies the durable harm as onlookers' impressions being hard to correct later.

codex_fields.name: Preemptive Accusation
codex_fields.why_this_matters: By the time the person speaks, the ground has been prepared, and an accurate account arrives sounding like retaliation for one already made.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Concerns raised in good faith often come first simply because that person noticed first. An honest observation can happen to precede a complaint by coincidence, and someone voicing a worry about you is not thereby anticipating one from you.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case makes the fair and important point that concerns raised in good faith often come first 'simply because that person noticed first' — which prevents sequence alone from being treated as evidence. It also excludes someone voicing a worry about you as thereby anticipating one from you. The why identifies why an accurate account then sounds like retaliation.

codex_fields.name: Complaint Weaponization
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Whichever account reaches the record first tends to set the frame, so a truthful second report is read as a response rather than as information.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Reporting a real concern promptly through proper channels is exactly what people are told to do, and someone unaware of how quick reporting can look is acting in good faith. Both parties independently reporting close in time, neither knowing about the other, is common.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case protects exactly the right thing: reporting a real concern promptly through proper channels 'is exactly what people are told to do'. Without that, the entry would discourage prompt reporting, which would be a genuine harm. It also notes both parties independently reporting close in time is common. The why identifies the framing advantage of whichever account reaches the record first.

codex_fields.name: Counterfeit Calm
codex_fields.why_this_matters: A proportionate emotional response gets read as instability by contrast, leaving a person to choose between being upset and being credible.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Even-keeled people exist, and staying steady under stress is a real and often hard-won skill. Choosing to stay calm in order to de-escalate a conflict is helpful rather than dismissive. Cultural and personal norms favouring composure are widespread, and none of that requires anyone else to be reactive.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case is thorough and fair, protecting even-keeled people, staying steady under stress as 'a real and often hard-won skill', deliberate de-escalation, and cultural norms favouring composure — and closing with the key point that none of that requires anyone else to be reactive. The why identifies the genuine bind of choosing between being upset and being credible.

codex_fields.name: Double Binds
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Every available response is wrong, so effort produces fault whatever is chosen, and a person begins to conclude the problem must be themselves.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Two pieces of feedback about genuinely different situations can feel contradictory when set side by side, and preferences shift over time without anyone laying a trap. Someone hard to please out of their own dissatisfaction is not necessarily constructing a no-win.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case correctly allows that two pieces of feedback about genuinely different situations can feel contradictory side by side and that preferences shift over time 'without anyone laying a trap'. It also distinguishes someone hard to please from someone constructing a no-win. The why identifies the self-attribution that follows: the person begins to conclude the problem must be themselves.

codex_fields.name: Role Reversal Traps
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The person who was harmed ends up doing the comforting and then the apologising, so accountability finishes further from the harm than where it started.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Genuine remorse often includes real distress, and someone overwhelmed by their own mistake may need a moment without expecting to be looked after. Mutual reassurance is a normal part of repair between two people who were both affected.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case makes the clinically sound point that genuine remorse often includes real distress and that someone overwhelmed by their own mistake 'may need a moment without expecting to be looked after'. That protects real contrition from being read as manipulation. Mutual reassurance is correctly named as a normal part of repair. The why identifies that accountability finishes further from the harm than where it started.

codex_fields.name: Sarcasm as Weapon
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Criticism lands in full while objecting to it means arguing about a joke, so the hurt has nowhere to go.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Mutual, affectionate teasing that both people enjoy is not this, and a generally sarcastic style applied evenly to everyone has no particular target. One sharp remark in a bad moment, acknowledged and not repeated, is friction rather than a pattern.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case correctly protects mutual affectionate teasing that both people enjoy and a generally sarcastic style applied evenly, with targeting as the discriminator. Treating one sharp remark in a bad moment, acknowledged and not repeated, as friction rather than a pattern is the right threshold. The why identifies the specific bind: objecting means arguing about a joke, so the hurt has nowhere to go.

codex_fields.name: Public Humiliation
codex_fields.why_this_matters: An audience makes the injury durable in a way private criticism is not: everyone present carries a version of it afterwards, including the person it was about.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Necessary and time-sensitive feedback sometimes has to be given where others happen to be, and settings where feedback is normal and applied evenly to everybody are humiliating nobody. An awkward moment can be nothing more than poor timing.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case is fair to real workplace and teaching contexts, conceding that necessary and time-sensitive feedback sometimes has to be given where others happen to be, and that settings where feedback is normal and evenly applied humiliate nobody. An awkward moment is correctly allowed to be poor timing. The why identifies the durability an audience creates.

codex_fields.name: Labeling as Identity Warfare
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Once a label attaches, ordinary behaviour gets read as confirming it, so there is no conduct available that would disprove it.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: An unflattering characterisation can be accurate, based on a real and consistent pattern. Reputations also form organically when many people independently have similar experiences. Specific feedback about a specific behaviour is a different thing from a defect label that stands in for the whole person.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case makes the essential concession that an unflattering characterisation can be accurate and based on a real pattern, and that reputations form organically when many people independently have similar experiences. The distinction between specific feedback about a behaviour and a defect label standing in for the whole person is the right one. The why identifies the unfalsifiability: no conduct is available that would disprove it.

codex_fields.name: Rage as Control
codex_fields.why_this_matters: People around an outburst learn to prioritise de-escalation over whatever point set it off, so the topic stops being raised long before anyone consciously decides to stop raising it.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Proportionate anger at something genuinely upsetting, expressed and then resolved without changing the outcome of the conversation, is ordinary. Someone actively working on emotional regulation is not using it as leverage. A single outburst during unusual stress, acknowledged afterwards, is not a pattern.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case is clinically careful in a way that matters, protecting someone 'actively working on emotional regulation' from being read as using anger as leverage, and treating a single outburst during unusual stress, acknowledged afterwards, as not a pattern. The why is well framed on function rather than intent — people learn to prioritise de-escalation 'long before anyone consciously decides to stop raising it' — which correctly matches the source's point that rage need not be performed cynically to operate as control.

codex_fields.name: Credit Theft
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Work continues while recognition for it accrues elsewhere, and by the time the pattern is visible the original attribution is too old to establish.

The why identifies the evidentiary decay problem: by the time the pattern is visible, the original attribution is too old to establish.

codex_fields.name: Sabotaging Success

codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Coincidence is real, and unrelated circumstances often land at inconvenient moments. Some people are unreliable across the board rather than at particular moments. Genuinely competing constraints can clash with someone's timeline while having nothing to do with it.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case leads with the right correction — 'coincidence is real' — which is the necessary deflation for an entry built entirely on timing. It also distinguishes people who are unreliable across the board from people unreliable at particular moments, which is the correct discriminator. The why identifies the self-attribution error: doubting one's competence rather than the timing.

codex_fields.name: Impossible Metrics

codex_fields.what_it_is_not: High but achievable standards that others in the same role have actually met are demanding rather than impossible.
