codex_fields.name: Half-Truth Framing
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Every fact checks out individually, so a listener who verifies carefully still arrives at the wrong conclusion.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: An accurate summary necessarily omits detail for length. People often present facts in whatever order those facts occurred to them. A genuinely different, honestly held interpretation of the same true facts is disagreement rather than arrangement.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case correctly protects an accurate summary that necessarily omits detail for length, and people presenting facts 'in whatever order those facts occurred to them' — a realistic and easily missed alternative to strategic arrangement. Distinguishing a genuinely different honest interpretation as disagreement rather than arrangement is the right final exclusion. The why identifies that careful verification still yields the wrong conclusion.

codex_fields.name: False Reports
codex_fields.why_this_matters: A fabricated complaint puts a real job, licence or family arrangement in jeopardy, and the person has to answer for something that did not happen before anyone establishes whether it did.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: A genuine report that characterises events in a way the subject disputes still reflects the reporter's honest perception. Institutions make their own errors in processing legitimate reports. Two people can disagree factually about what happened without either one inventing anything.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case does essential work: a genuine report that characterises events in a way the subject disputes 'still reflects the reporter's honest perception'. Without that, this entry would be usable to reframe any unwelcome complaint as fabricated, which is a serious misuse risk in this subject area. Institutional processing errors and genuine factual disagreement are also excluded. The why identifies the burden of answering before anything is established.

codex_fields.name: Paper-Trail Traps
codex_fields.why_this_matters: A record accumulates that the person has no opportunity to answer as it is built, and by the time they see it, it reads as damning.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Standard documentation applied to everyone is not targeting. A genuine record of concerns that were actually raised with the person is legitimate even if they wish it did not exist. Someone keeping notes on their own experience for their own reference is doing something ordinary.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case correctly protects standard documentation applied to everyone as 'not targeting', a genuine record of concerns actually raised with the person 'even if they wish it did not exist', and someone keeping notes on their own experience. That third exclusion matters, since people in difficult situations are routinely advised to document. The why identifies the specific unfairness of a record built without opportunity to answer.

codex_fields.name: Compartmentalization
codex_fields.why_this_matters: No single person can see enough to raise a question, so accountability fails not because anyone refused it but because nobody had the view required to ask for it.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Confidentiality and need-to-know structures exist for genuinely good reasons in most organisations. Information silos form naturally in any large family or workplace. Someone who simply did not think to pass something on has partitioned nothing.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case correctly protects confidentiality and need-to-know structures that 'exist for genuinely good reasons in most organisations' and notes information silos form naturally in any large family or workplace. Someone who simply did not think to pass something on 'has partitioned nothing' is a clean exclusion. The why identifies the distinctive failure: accountability fails not because anyone refused it but because nobody had the view required to ask.

codex_fields.name: Thought Control
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The vocabulary available for examining the situation is itself supplied from inside it, so doubt arrives already labelled as a symptom.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Every group develops shared shorthand over time, and that is normal rather than controlling. Beliefs a person holds independently and can give their own reasons for are theirs. Passionate, sincerely held conviction is a different thing from a mechanism that suppresses dissent.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case is the necessary guard on a Lifton-derived entry and it is well made: every group develops shared shorthand 'and that is normal rather than controlling', beliefs a person can give their own reasons for are theirs, and passionate sincere conviction is distinguished from a mechanism that suppresses dissent. The why identifies the recursive trap precisely — the vocabulary for examining the situation is supplied from inside it, so doubt arrives already labelled as a symptom.

codex_fields.name: Phobia Indoctrination
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Avoidance becomes bodily rather than reasoned, so options stay ruled out by a fear response that persists even after the person has concluded the fear was unwarranted.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Proportionate warnings about real risks, from someone with relevant experience, are useful information. Pre-existing anxiety or trauma responses belong to the person and may have nothing to do with anyone currently present. Cautious family or cultural norms can be restrictive without having been constructed to frighten anyone.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case protects proportionate warnings about real risks from someone with relevant experience, and — the clinically important one — states that pre-existing anxiety or trauma responses 'belong to the person and may have nothing to do with anyone currently present'. That guards against a reader attributing their own history to a current partner, which is the dominant misapplication risk here and runs opposite to the usual direction. Cautious cultural norms are also excluded. The why is accurate that the fear response persists after the person has concluded it was unwarranted.

codex_fields.name: Administrative Escalation
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Defending against a disproportionate process consumes time, money and attention regardless of how it concludes, and the next concern goes unraised for that reason alone.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Some issues genuinely warrant formal process regardless of who raised a concern first. Organisations and families with a low threshold for formalising things apply it evenly to everyone. Someone unaware that informal resolution was available may escalate simply from not knowing another route existed.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case correctly protects issues that genuinely warrant formal process 'regardless of who raised a concern first', organisations with a low threshold for formalising things applied evenly, and someone escalating simply from not knowing an informal route existed. That third exclusion is realistic and generous. The why identifies that the defending cost lands regardless of how the process concludes.

codex_fields.name: Paper Terrorism
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Burden accumulates across filings rather than sitting in any one of them: responding to all of them costs time and money whether or not a single one has merit.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Genuinely complex disputes require multiple legitimate filings to resolve. Thorough counsel generates volume as a by-product of diligence rather than as a strategy. Institutions produce a great deal of paperwork through their own procedural requirements, independent of any party's conduct.
codex_fields.note: The short_definition is truncated mid-list ("...floods of filings, motions, complaints,."), so both fields were derived from the expanded_definition and false-positive list instead.
codex_fields.review_note: PRIORITY. The draft_note correctly flags the truncated source definition and explains the derivation from the expanded definition and false-positive list. The why correctly locates the mechanism in accumulation rather than in any single filing — 'responding to all of them costs time and money whether or not a single one has merit' — which is the accurate account and avoids asserting that any particular filing is meritless. The disconfirming case protects genuinely complex disputes, thorough counsel generating volume as a by-product of diligence, and institutions' own procedural paperwork. This is a purely exculpatory list without a closing discriminator, which I note as part of a broader structural pattern in the report, but the stakes here are procedural rather than personal-safety and the why carries the distinguishing point, so it does not cross into a revision.

codex_fields.name: Brigading
codex_fields.why_this_matters: Volume arriving at once removes any possibility of responding the way a single message could be answered, and the platform itself becomes unusable for as long as it lasts.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: Virality is not coordination: a post that spreads on its own draws unconnected people who arrived by different routes. What marks this pattern is convergence traceable to a single rallying post or thread — and several friends reacting to the same thing independently is not that.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case makes the correct central distinction — 'virality is not coordination' — and identifies what would mark the difference: convergence traceable to a single rallying post or thread. Explicitly excluding several friends reacting to the same thing independently closes the most likely over-read. The why identifies both the impossibility of proportionate response and the platform becoming unusable.

codex_fields.name: Context Collapse Exploitation
codex_fields.why_this_matters: The version that circulates is the stripped one, and restoring the context means reaching an audience that has already reacted.
codex_fields.what_it_is_not: People misunderstand context themselves and pass things on innocently. Headlines and short excerpts truncate longer statements as a matter of format. Sharing something without checking where it came from is careless rather than exploitative.
codex_fields.review_note: The disconfirming case is fair on all three and the third is the most useful: sharing something without checking where it came from is 'careless rather than exploitative', which correctly separates negligence from design. Headlines and short excerpts truncating longer statements as a matter of format is also properly excluded. The why identifies the asymmetry that restoring context means reaching an audience that has already reacted.
